facts.f: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
facts.e: He was the first non-European to win a Nobel Prize in Literature, for Gitanjali.

facts.f: Rabindranath Tagore wrote the national anthems of both India and Bangladesh.
facts.e: India's is 'Jana Gana Mana' and Bangladesh's is 'Amar Shonar Bangla'.

facts.f: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci.
facts.e: It hangs in the Louvre Museum in Paris.

facts.f: Vincent van Gogh painted 'The Starry Night' in 1889.
facts.e: It shows a swirling night sky over a village.

facts.f: Raja Ravi Varma was a famous Indian painter of the 1800s.
facts.e: He is known for oil paintings of scenes from Indian epics, and his prints reached homes across India.

facts.f: The Ajanta and Ellora caves in Maharashtra are cut into solid rock.
facts.e: Ajanta is famous for ancient paintings, and Ellora for its carved temples.

facts.f: Madhubani painting comes from the Mithila region of Bihar.
facts.e: It uses bright colours and patterns of nature, gods and village life.

facts.f: Warli painting is a tribal art from Maharashtra.
facts.e: It uses simple circles, triangles and lines to show people and daily life.

facts.f: Kalidasa was a great Sanskrit poet and playwright.
facts.e: His works include the play Abhijnanashakuntalam and the poem Meghaduta, in which a cloud carries a message.

facts.f: Valmiki is traditionally known as the author of the Ramayana, and Vyasa of the Mahabharata.
facts.e: Valmiki is called the 'Adi Kavi', the first poet.

facts.f: Munshi Premchand was a great writer in Hindi and Urdu.
facts.e: His stories include 'Idgah', and his novels include 'Godaan'.

facts.f: William Shakespeare wrote plays like Romeo and Juliet, Hamlet and Macbeth.
facts.e: He lived in England about 400 years ago.

facts.f: The Panchatantra is a collection of ancient Indian animal fables.
facts.e: It is traditionally said to have been written by Vishnu Sharma to teach wisdom to young princes.

facts.f: Indian music has seven basic notes: Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha and Ni.
facts.e: These notes are called swaras.

facts.f: Indian classical music has two main traditions: Hindustani and Carnatic.
facts.e: Hindustani music is mostly from the north, and Carnatic music from the south.

facts.f: Pandit Ravi Shankar was a world-famous sitar player.
facts.e: He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

facts.f: Ustad Bismillah Khan was a master of the shehnai.
facts.e: He played the shehnai at the Red Fort on India's first Independence Day, 15 August 1947.

facts.f: M. S. Subbulakshmi was the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna, in 1998.
facts.e: She was a great singer of Carnatic music.

facts.f: Ludwig van Beethoven kept composing great music even after he became deaf.
facts.e: His Ninth Symphony was written when he could hardly hear at all.

facts.f: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart began composing music at the age of five.
facts.e: He wrote more than 600 works in his short life.

facts.f: A standard piano has 88 keys.
facts.e: 52 are white and 36 are black.

facts.f: In painting, red, yellow and blue are called the primary colours.
facts.e: They can be mixed to make secondary colours like orange, green and purple.

facts.f: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper.
facts.e: The paper crane is one of the most famous origami shapes.

facts.f: Satyajit Ray was a great Indian film-maker.
facts.e: His first film, Pather Panchali (1955), won awards around the world. He received an honorary Oscar in 1992.

facts.f: Raja Harishchandra (1913), made by Dadasaheb Phalke, was India's first full-length feature film.
facts.e: It was a silent film. India's first sound film, Alam Ara, came in 1931.

facts.f: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest award in cinema.
facts.e: It is named after the father of Indian cinema.

facts.f: The Jnanpith Award is one of India's highest literary awards.
facts.e: The first Jnanpith Award was given in 1965 to the Malayalam poet G. Sankara Kurup.

facts.f: The Tirukkural is a Tamil classic written by Thiruvalluvar.
facts.e: It has 1,330 short couplets about virtue, wealth and love.

facts.f: Michelangelo painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in Vatican City.
facts.e: It took him about four years.

facts.f: Pablo Picasso helped start a style of art called Cubism.
facts.e: Cubist paintings show objects from many angles at once, using geometric shapes.

facts.f: 'The Thinker' is a famous bronze sculpture by Auguste Rodin.
facts.e: It shows a man sitting deep in thought, with his chin on his hand.

facts.f: Rangoli and kolam are colourful patterns drawn on floors and doorsteps.
facts.e: They are made with coloured powder, rice flour or flower petals, especially at festivals.

facts.f: Kathputli is the traditional string-puppet art of Rajasthan.
facts.e: Puppeteers move wooden puppets with strings while telling stories with songs.

facts.f: Kalamkari is a traditional art of hand-painting or block-printing on cloth.
facts.e: It comes from Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. 'Kalam' means pen.

facts.f: Tanjore paintings from Tamil Nadu are known for their gold foil.
facts.e: They are bright, richly decorated paintings, often of gods.

facts.f: R. K. Narayan created the imaginary South Indian town of Malgudi.
facts.e: His book 'Swami and Friends' is set there.

facts.f: An orchestra has four main sections: strings, woodwind, brass and percussion.
facts.e: The conductor leads them all with a baton.

facts.f: Kathak is a classical dance of storytelling.
facts.e: Its name comes from 'katha', which means story.

facts.f: The Bhagavad Gita is part of the Mahabharata.
facts.e: It is a conversation between Krishna and Arjuna on a battlefield.

facts.f: Sarojini Naidu, a poet and freedom fighter, was called the 'Nightingale of India'.
facts.e: She was also the first woman Governor of an Indian state.

facts.f: The sitar, veena and sarod are string instruments. The tabla and mridangam are drums.
facts.e: The bansuri is a bamboo flute.

facts.f: Amrita Sher-Gil is one of India's most celebrated modern painters.
facts.e: Her paintings showed everyday Indian life, especially women.

quiz.q: Who created the town of Malgudi?
quiz.x: Malgudi is an imaginary town in his stories.

quiz.x: Michelangelo painted it over about four years.

quiz.q: How many keys does a standard piano have?

quiz.x: It has 1,330 couplets.

quiz.q: Warli art comes from which state?
quiz.x: Warli art uses simple shapes to show daily life.

quiz.q: Which are the three primary colours in painting?
quiz.x: Green, orange and purple are secondary colours made by mixing them.

quiz.x: Kalidasa wrote in Sanskrit.

quiz.q: Which composer kept writing music after becoming deaf?
quiz.x: Beethoven wrote his Ninth Symphony when he was almost completely deaf.

quiz.x: Origami means 'folding paper' in Japanese.

quiz.x: Sarojini Naidu was a poet and freedom fighter.
